$comment: THE 2002 LANGUAGE ELEMENT STANDINGS, held once as data (kb/Work PB4993, PB5256; DESIGN-spec-conformance-review.md
section 10.2): the archaic language elements of §2002:G.1, which §2002:3.1.10 defines, and the obsolete language
elements of §2002:G.2, which §2002:3.1.11 defines. The shape is the 1985 file's (spec-element-standing-1985.json, whose
comment states each key). A section is the element's SPECIFICATION; OWN or SHARED is derived from its heading
(element_standing.own). Annex A, the communications facility, is the obsolete element of G.2 entry 1 whole (its
region is the annex, `A`, from its title heading). Continuation of COBOL words (G.1 entry 1) is specified in the prose
of §2002:6.2.4, outside any rule block while the content-keyed manifest holds that clause pending. MOVE of
alphanumeric figurative constants to numeric items (G.1 entry 2) is named by the note of the MOVE statement's general
rule on the category of figurative constants. `remarks` names the sections whose standing sentence is not an
element's specification: the processor-dependent element list (B.3) and the informative concepts annex (E.5).
extract_rule_catalog.py applies the lists (each rule's `status`) and records any disagreement as a finding.

remarks.why: none: every archaic-element sentence of the text is in a section an entry names

remarks.why: the processor-dependent element list and the informative concepts annex
